title: S. P. Kothari — Accrual Accounting Process: Part I, MIT 15.511 (11 June 2004)
use: Debit and credit sides, account normal balances, temporary equity accounts, journal-to-ledger posting, trial balance and errors consistent with equal columns.
verification: Opened the actual 33-page MIT PDF and inspected the title/date and slides 2–20 and 28–33, including the debit/credit and account classification conventions, journal/ledger sequence, retained-earnings role and limits of a trial balance. The official Summer 2004 course lecture-notes catalogue identifies Kothari as instructor. All Harbor amounts, events, exercises and worked cases are original; the source bakery case is not reproduced. These historical teaching mechanics do not establish current GAAP/IFRS compliance.

title: S. P. Kothari — Accrual Accounting Process: Part II, MIT 15.511 (14 June 2003; hosted in Summer 2004 materials)
use: Period-end accruals/deferrals, supplies and insurance consumption, customer advances, unpaid wages/interest, depreciation and its contra asset.
verification: Opened the actual 52-page PDF; title says Summer 2003 and June 14, 2003 even though the hosting course is Summer 2004. Inspected slides 11–18 on timing/adjustment, 19–29 on wage/interest accruals, 30–41 on supplies/prepaids/advances, and 42–51 on depreciation and accumulated depreciation. The chapter scopes its own six noncash adjustments and does not import blanket statements that every closing correction excludes Cash, that matching overrides asset recognition, or that dated notes settle current reporting requirements. Original supplied schedules make the amounts determinate.

title: IFRS Foundation — Conceptual Framework Project Summary (March 2018)
use: Distinguish element definitions, recognition and measurement; owner movements versus income/expense; conceptual guidance versus a binding transaction-specific standard.
verification: Opened the actual publicly accessible 20-page publisher summary. Inspected page 2 for the Framework not being a Standard and not overriding Standards; pages 6–10 for qualitative characteristics, entity, assets/liabilities/equity and recognition; and pages 11–13 for derecognition/measurement context. An attempted issued-Framework PDF led to registration/premium access, so no inspection of that full text is claimed; the cited source is the separate legitimate public March 2018 summary. The manuscript makes no current jurisdictional compliance or blanket GAAP/IFRS equivalence claim and reproduces no actual company observations.
